newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares end higher for fifth day,fund buying.
newsitem.headline: India shares end higher for fifth day,fund buying.

text.p: Indian blue chips closed higher on Wednesday on the back of foreign fund buying, as the market's winning streak continued to remain strong for the fifth straight session.
Traders said the rally in share prices was led by frontline stocks such as ACC, Hindustan Lever, Colgate, Nestle and Tata Tea, with a few second-tier stocks also taking part.

"The rally has spread to side-counters, but the market looks a bit dangerous now," said Purvesh Shah, chief dealer at Nucleus Securities in Bombay. Bombay's 30-share index has jumped 176 points, or five percent in the last five consecutive sessions.
Much of the surge in buying interest has come from foreign funds, analysts said, adding that funds were picking up blue chips despite a long pending delay in an increase in government-set oil prices.
"Funds are keen buyers in their select universe of stocks," said a dealer at a foreign firm. "The price hike has been pushed to the backgound, at least for the time-being."
Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said on Tuesday his United Front coalition's policy-setting steering committee will take a decision on petroleum product prices on June 15.

Analysts said the government must decide soon how to pay the money it owes to oil companies -- a total of 155 billion rupees ($4.33 billion) at the end of March -- for selling subsidised petroleum products well below global prices.
"Yes, the oil price hike has been discounted, but the minute it comes, the market is bound to adjust," said Ajay Srinivasan, chief investment officer at ITC-Threadneedle Asset Management.

"I think if it's done and done quickly, it shows the government's resolve to tackle important problems," Srinivasan said. "By delaying it, they are only sending a message that they are not facing the issue upfront."
